chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashem, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma'bad, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abil Hassan Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him)

He said: 'Looking at our progeny is worship.' They asked him: 'O son of God's Prophet, is looking at the Imams from among you worship, or is looking at all the progeny of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) worship?' He replied: 'Rather, looking at all the progeny of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is worship as long as they have not deviated from his path and have not become impure by committing sins.'

key_terms.مِنْهَاجَهُ: His path or way (referring to the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Is looking at the Prophet's descendants considered worship in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Musa al-Ridha clarifying that the virtue of 'gazing' (a sign of reverence and recognition) extends to all *Banu Hashim* and Prophet's descendants, not exclusively the Twelve Imams, provided they adhere to the prophetic methodology. This distinction highlights the Shia concept of *Zawaj al-Nubuwwa* (prophetic lineage) as a source of spiritual merit, linking physical reverence to moral integrity and freedom from major sins.
